newsitem.title: USA: U S West sees steady phone line growth.
newsitem.headline: U S West sees steady phone line growth.

text.p: U S West Inc's telephone line growth is expected to continue at its recent pace, Chief Financial Officer Allan Spies said Friday.

The Denver-based telephone company in its second quarter earnings report said access line growth stood at 4.6 percent over the past 12 months. Spies in a telephone interview said the recent rate of growth was expected to "hold."
Last year the rate was 5 percent, reflecting the peak of recent growth in the Rocky Mountain region. Before the population boom, access line growth was around was 3-4 percent, he said.

The heavy growth also took a toll on the phone company's service record when U S West Telecommunications was unable to fill customer orders in an acceptable time frame. But Spies said the company has shown a 37 percent improvement over last year and a 65 percent improvement over 1995 in filling orders for primary service.

U S West Communications Chief Executive Officer Sol Trujillo has vowed to improve customer service and Spies conceded that it will be a while before the company puts the poor installment service reputation behind it. "We will have to continue to improve," Spies said.

He also said the company's plan to sell some $1 billion in selected rural exchanges is expected to be completed by the "third or fourth quarter" of this year. The plan was first announced in 1993. In the just-completed second quarter U S West realized an $18 million after tax gain from selling rural exchanges in Idaho, Iowa and South Dakota.
